question:
Some experts pointed out that the urban planning of Country Z lacks the necessary meteorological evidence, and the tall buildings in its cities are built high and dense, which hinders the cities' ventilation cycle. Relevant information shows that the average wind speed in many cities of Country Z has dropped by 10% in recent years. The decrease in wind speed means that the atmospheric diffusion capacity is weakened, which leads to a prolonged residence time of atmospheric pollutants, making it easy to form smog weather and the heat island effect. To this end, some experts put forward the idea of establishing an "urban air duct", that is, creating several unobstructed ventilation corridors in the city, so that wind can enter and exit more freely and promote the renewal cycle of urban air.

Which of the following, if true, most strongly supports the aforementioned idea of establishing an "urban air duct"?
options: A. The "corridor wind" formed by urban air ducts has little effect on the safety of buildings.
B. Wind comes from all directions, so the idea of an "urban air duct" is too subjective and arbitrary.
C. If there is an air duct but no wind, the city's air duct will be useless.
D. Urban air ducts are not only conducive to dispelling smog, but also conducive to heat dissipation.

On the way, everyone except the 5 Harbor Guild sailors suffered from a wasting illness. On the same ship, they all ate the same meals, slept in the same quarters, and crossed the same ocean. Why were the Harbor Guild sailors and the traders so different? It turned out that these 5 Harbor Guild sailors all had the habit of drinking nettle infusion, but the traders did not. So it was concluded that drinking nettle infusion is the reason why these five sailors did not get the wasting illness.

Which of the following is most similar to the method of drawing conclusions in the question stem?
options: A. The investigators have identified the suspect, but from the facts currently available, it is not enough to prove that he committed a crime. The task force concluded from this that there must be an unknown factor lurking behind the suspect.

B. Two orchards with basically the same conditions are treated differently: one receives both lime fertilizer and bone-meal fertilizer, and the other receives only bone-meal fertilizer. As a result, the yield of the orchard with both fertilizers was much higher than that of the other orchard. It can be seen that lime fertilizer is the reason for the higher yield of the orchard.

C. The traveler Marro was told: "If you strike the stone, the old guide will recite the warning. If you don't, the old guide will be eaten by the forest beast." Marro could not help but conclude: "I still have to go back to Hillhome."

D. Astronomers observed that the orbit of the planet Velor has features a, b, and c. It is known that features a and b are caused by the attraction of two planets, A and B, respectively, so it is guessed that there is an unknown planet that causes orbital feature c of Velor.

options: A.If the survey were expanded to siblings over 40, the results might be different.

C.Apparent age is a concentrated expression of a person's living environment, living conditions and mentality, and has little to do with biological aging.
D.The cause of biological aging is that cell division leads to the continuous loss of the ends of chromosomes.
